capability.summary: Run Vulture on one Python file or directory and return candidate dead-code lines
capability.description: Executes exactly `[vulture, target]`, splits non-empty stdout lines into findings, and reports their count and Vulture exit code. It statically identifies candidates using Vulture defaults and does not execute or modify target code.
capability.problem_space: Read-only Vulture candidate discovery for unused Python definitions and unreachable code; not proof that code is safe to delete, general linting, type checking, security analysis, execution, or automated cleanup.

constraint.io_signature: Input: required file_path string naming an existing Python file or directory. Executes `vulture <target>` with inherited cwd and Vulture defaults. Output: JSON envelope containing exit_code, dead_code_count, findings lines, and stderr.
accepted_inputs: an existing directory tree intended for Vulture static analysis
constraint.output_shape: After Vulture returns: {status: "success", tool: "vulture", target: string, exit_code: integer, dead_code_count: integer, findings: [string], stderr: string|null}; the wrapper exits 0 regardless of Vulture exit code. Missing target: {status: "error", message: string}, exit 2. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON. Missing executable, 120-second timeout, or subprocess launch failure is uncaught and may traceback without JSON.
limitations: Vulture reports heuristic candidates and can produce false positives for dynamic imports, reflection, framework callbacks, decorators, plugins, and externally referenced APIs
uses only Vulture defaults with no confidence, exclude, ignore-name, or sort options and returns raw finding lines rather than parsed symbols
does not execute or modify code, remove findings, run a linter/type checker, or prove that removal is behaviorally safe
uses a fixed 120-second subprocess timeout that is not caught into JSON and applies no finding or output truncation

output_contract.description: JSON envelope containing Vulture's candidate finding lines, count, exit code, and stderr; no code is changed.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: find candidate unused Python code with Vulture
scan a Python file or directory for dead code candidates
negative_intents: delete or automatically clean dead Python code
prove code is unreachable or safe to remove
run Ruff Flake8 Bandit or execute Python code
